observations.text: Scope of this re-review: S2 bytes at commit 7b86b74 with a clean working tree (git status --porcelain empty). Changes since the last S2 approval (ad7687c) are 808ebd2 (REPOS_READ_WORDINGS and SCAN_AGAIN moved from the oracle file into tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs, values byte-identical: ["repos read","repo read"] and "Scan again") and 25f0df8 (new scenario a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read_without_an_account). The support diff also carries show_repos_read and restart_refusing, which S2 does not use; they were judged under S1 and are not reassessed here.

Oracle run as it stands. argv: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/fix-repos-read-truthful/target-ad cargo test --offline -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_legacy_run_repos_read. exit 0, stderr carried only cargo progress. stdout: 'running 6 tests ... test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 2.86s' - the four S2 scenarios (a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read, ..._without_an_account, a_scan_that_read_the_repos_it_planned_says_how_many, a_scan_that_could_read_none_of_the_repos_it_planned_still_says_so) plus two support self-tests. The file collects and builds from the project's native runner with declared dependencies only.

Semantic RED observed by this reviewer, not reused. I re-injected the wrong behaviour the new scenario names: crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs:316, the None arm of imports_only_summary, changed from NO_ACCOUNT_TO_RECHECK.to_string() to format!("{NO_ACCOUNT_TO_RECHECK} 0 repos read"). Same argv as the green run; exit 101. stdout: 'test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed', the one failure being a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read_without_an_account, panicking at tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs:108 with 'WHAT: her queue says "repos read" for a run kept before any scan plan was stored.' This is the promised outcome being wrong, not an import, collection, fixture or startup failure. Production was restored with git checkout and byte-compared against a pre-mutation copy (identical); git status --porcelain is empty and the same command then passed 6/6 in 2.98s.

The new scenario is a distinct observation, not a duplicate of the plan-less scenario already approved. The queue has two completed-run summary builders in crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs: scan_summary_by_account (an owner with a verified account, exercised by the three earlier scenarios) and imports_only_summary (an owner with no account who imported a repo, exercised only by the new one). Under the injected defect in the second builder the three earlier scenarios stayed green while only the new one failed, so without it a run with no plan rows could still be told '0 repos read' on that page. Its guard phrase 'No GitHub account to re-check' is emitted nowhere else in the crates (grep over crates and tests: queue.rs:53 definition, 315 and 316 the only uses), and only for a Completed latest run, so the negative claim cannot pass vacuously on a page that would carry no count anyway.

P2 closure both ways. Promise P2 ('a completed run with no plan rows shows no repos-read line; a planned run keeps its true count') is falsifiable in both directions: hiding the line for a planned run is caught by a_scan_that_could_read_none_of_the_repos_it_planned_still_says_so (it asserts '0 repos read' beside the named archived repo that proves a plan row exists) and by a_scan_that_read_the_repos_it_planned_says_how_many ('5 repos read', the count compared with the repos the GitHub double was actually asked to read); showing a line for a plan-less run is caught by the two legacy-store scenarios, now on both summary builders. Every scenario drives the public HTTP pages through the signed-in browser and reads page text only; no store, private module or internal state is touched. Expectations E4 and E5 both have a falsifier. No oracle observation lacks a declared promise.

Order independence and timing. The new scenario run alone: argv as above plus '-- --exact a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read_without_an_account'; exit 0, 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 5 filtered out; finished in 2.63s'. The whole S2 binary finishes in about 2.9s, so no half-budget or derogation evidence is due and none is claimed.

Capability limits of this review. typesafe: unavailable - python .../nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output - exited 3, 'TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment', and the key is absent from a login shell too (zsh -lc check), so the oracle-critique questions (distinct observation, guard adequacy, public-port confinement) were decided locally from the run evidence above. code-fact query.reads-of NO_ACCOUNT_TO_RECHECK --root . did not finish within 120s on this repo root and I stopped the process I had started (exit 144); the locator fact was taken from grep over crates and tests, which is lexical and noisy, and was cross-checked against the two call sites read in queue.rs.

Non-blocking remark, no finding raised. docs/feature/fix-repos-read-truthful/acceptance.md section S2 names three test locators under its Disposition rows; the fourth scenario added by 25f0df8 is not named there. Coverage is a superset of what the manifest records and every scenario maps to the declared promise P2, so nothing is lost and no obligation is left without a falsifier. The acceptance designer may name it at the first covers block it belongs to, whenever that file is next edited.

diagnostic: Accepted. The revised S2 oracle is public, independent and complete for P2: it drives only the app's HTTP pages as a signed-in owner, asserts only what she reads there, and falsifies P2 in both directions - a plan-less run that invents a count, and a planned run that loses its count. The two changes since ad7687c are sound: the queue wordings moved into the shared support with byte-identical values, and the new scenario covers the second completed-run summary builder (imports_only_summary), which the three earlier scenarios cannot observe. I observed the semantic RED myself by re-injecting '0 repos read' into that builder's None arm: exit 101, exactly the new scenario failed at the repos-read assertion with its business-worded message while the other three stayed green; production was then restored byte-identical and the suite passed 6/6. No finding. Jev was unavailable (no API key) and one code-fact query timed out; both limits are recorded and neither left a judgment unsupported.
